title: Rava bar Rav Chanan
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Rabbah’s student from his youth, as in Berakhot 48b: Abaye and Rava [bar Rav Chanan, according to the Halakhot Gedolot’s reading] were sitting before Rabbah, and he asked them, “To whom do we bless?” They said to him, “To the Merciful One.” “And where does the Merciful One sit?” [Rava bar Rav Chanan] pointed to the roof … He said to them: “Both of you will become Rabbis.” Hyman explains in the entry Rava that this reading is the true one, for Rava’s place was in Mechoza, but Rava bar Rav Chanan was indeed in Pumbedita.

He was very dear to Rabbah, as in Shabbat 153a, when Abaye asked Rabbah, “Someone like the Master, whom they hate — who will warm the eulogy?” He said to him: “You and Rabbah bar Rav Chanan suffice” (Dikdukei Soferim: and Rava).
In Eruvin 92a: “Rabbah, Rabbi Zeira and Rabbah bar Rav Chanan were sitting, and Abaye was sitting with them.”

He was likewise Rav Yosef’s student, as in Eruvin 51b–52a: Rava bar Rav Chanan used to come from Artivna to Pumbedita (on Shabbat by means of an eruv) and say, “Let my resting place be at Tzinta” (he was going to Rav Yosef’s lecture — Rabbeinu Chananel). In Berakhot 45a he asked Rav Yosef. In Bava Batra 26a: Rava bar Rav Chanan had date palms at the edge of Rav Yosef’s orchard; birds would come and sit on the palm and come down into the orchard and cause damage. Rav Yosef asked him to cut them down, and he did not want to, and said to him, “If the Master wants to cut them, let him do so.” Hyman infers from this that his fixed place was in Pumbedita.

Likewise when Abaye headed the academy in Pumbedita, he sat with him and always discussed matters with him, as we find “Rava (or Rabbah) bar Rav Chanan said to Abaye,” as in Berakhot 45a; Shabbat 148a; Eruvin 14b, 38b, 45a, 51b, 68a, 73b, 75b, 86a and 93a; Pesachim 39a; Beitzah 30a; Ketubot 6b, 62a and 62b; Sanhedrin 60b and 61a; and Shevuot 18a. He called Abaye “Master,” as in Zevachim 110a, and also called him “tarda” (dullard), Keritot 18b, which Hyman attributes to their being true colleagues.
He was likewise Rava’s colleague, as in Menachot 40a and Chullin 129a.

We find in Zevachim 55a: “Rabbah bar Rav Chanan taught before Rava … Abaye said to him”; in Beitzah 12b, the host of Rava bar Rav Chanan asked him and he did not have [the answer]; he came before Rava … Abaye raised an objection to him; in Bava Kamma 55a Abaye resolves his difficulty; and there, 66b, he challenges Rav Yosef, and Rava gives the resolution.
Likewise Rav Avya was his colleague, as in Kiddushin 39a, where they supplied one another [with produce of uncertain orlah status].

notes.text: p004 is held for the missing footnote[1]. צינתא is Tzinta, a specific place in returned Rashi Eruvin51b, not shade; the52a continuation contains the quoted resting-place phrase. תרדא is the address dullard, not beet; the returned Keritot18b speaker is Rabbah bar barChana versus Hyman’s Rava barChanan, preserved as a variant. Saved Kiddushin39a has the pair SUPPLYING PRODUCE of uncertain orlah status to each other, not posing doubts. Hyman’s barChanan identification of the boy remains his claim.

The earlier note records the review before the missing footnote was recovered. The Wikisource editor’s footnote explains that Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 1059) mistakenly gives 51a. The journey appears at the end of Eruvin 51b and the declaration at the start of 52a. The consulted text calls the traveler Rabbah bar Rav Chanan and has him travel from Artibbena to Pumbedita. Rashi identifies Tzinta as a particular place between the two Shabbat limits. Rabbeinu Chananel describes Rava bar Chanan traveling from Antioch to hear Rav Yosef’s lecture and leaves the town where he would rest unnamed.

The exchange about the blessing appears in Berakhot 48a in the consulted text, where Rava has no patronymic. The Warsaw 1874 edition of Halakhot Gedolot (1:129) names Rava bar Rav Chanin. The identification of the boy as the subject of this entry and the argument from the two sages’ places of residence are Hyman’s.

In the consulted Keritot 18b, the exchange about an uncertain transgression includes versions that name Rava bar Chanan and Rava. The retort to Abaye using tarda, “dullard,” is attributed there to Rabbah bar bar Chana. Hyman attributes it to the subject of this entry.

The printed Hyman (vol. III, p. 1059) reads ורבא מתרץ לו, “and Rava gives the resolution,” where the supplied transcription reads ורב. Bava Kamma 66b gives Rava’s resolution and separately credits Rav Yosef with an earlier answer to a question that had troubled Rabbah. In the consulted Zevachim 55a, Rava raises the objection that Hyman attributes to Abaye. Abaye raises the objection in the separate exchange in Beitzah 12b.
